newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, gains precarious.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, gains precarious.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished higher on Wednesday but below a key resistance level, which would have signalled further gains in the near term.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 245 points higher at 18,440 after hitting a high of 18,540.
A dealer with a Japanese house said active buying of Nikkei futures in Osaka lifted the SIMEX contract early in the day.

"I think the market should come down tomorrow. It's looking a bit toppish below 18,600," he said, adding that players who bought the contract earlier would look to cash in their gains towards the 18,700 level.
Another trader said a close above the 18,500 level would be a bullish sign, bringing the 19,500 target back into view.
He said the market looked supported around 18,150 in the short term, but a failure to close above 18,500 this week would expose the March Nikkei to a test of the 17,500 level.
Dealers said there was no fresh news out of Japan affecting the market and the dollar's renewed rise above 124 yen in Tokyo trade had no impact.
But a breach of the 125 yen target, which is priced in, was likely to hurt the Nikkei as it would raise fears of imports being hit, they said.
The March MSCI Taiwan stock index contract ended at 315.6 against its opening 316.5 on volume of 315 lots.
